candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — medication-error prevention and reporting
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize and report look-alike drug labeling or packaging as a preventable medication-safety hazard before an error occurs.

options.A: Ignore the similarity until a wrong-drug event actually occurs.
options.B: Report the look-alike packaging as a medication-error hazard through the appropriate safety process.
options.C: Assume the packaging is safe because both products are FDA approved.
options.D: Rely only on memory to distinguish the products during administration.

candidate.rationale: FDA identifies look-alike container labels as a preventable medication-error hazard and encourages reporting of medication errors and circumstances that may cause or lead to an error, including look-alike labels. A safety concern should therefore be reported before harm occurs. B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Look-alike container labels can cause preventable wrong-drug errors, and FDA encourages reporting of circumstances such as look-alike labels that may cause or lead to medication errors.
candidate.source_document_title: Medication Errors Related to CDER-Regulated Drug Products
candidate.source_locator: Medication-error definition/examples; postapproval monitoring and reporting — look-alike container labels
candidate.stem: A nurse notices that two different medications have very similar container labels and packaging. No error has occurred yet. What is the best action?
